title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Arkadiankadun siltaremontti aiheuttaa muutoksia liikennejärjestelyihin Luonnontieteellisen museon lähistöllä
content:
The renovation will start with the construction of temporary traffic arrangements from Wednesday 7 January onwards. The renovation is expected to be completed in late 2026.

A temporary bridge for pedestrians will be built on the east side of Arkadiankatu over the Baana. The aim is to maintain the pedestrian route on the east side of the bridge until the temporary bridge is operational. Cyclists will also be able to use the bridge.

The Baana route underneath the bridge is expected to remain open for most of the renovation's duration, with some minor exceptions.

There will be changes to the motor vehicle routes by the bridge and around it in January. If possible, should be favoured during the bridge renovation.

Connections to the bus terminals in Kamppi will remain available, but there will be a slight diversion of routes.

Trams 1 and 1T will run via Simonkatu and Kamppi. Lasipalatsi and the Natural History Museum will not be served.

The diversion is due to the renovation of the Arkadiankatu bridge and will remain in place until late 2026. The renovation will not affect HSL's bus services.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Conference greetings: ESA conference 2026
content:
This year’s European Sociology Association conference was held in Warsaw, Poland on 25-28 August. CEACG’s researchers Mark Tarplee, Michael Egerer, Veera Kankainen, and Sébastien Berret took part in the conference and contributed with their presentations. 

The conference brought together over 3000 sociologists from all over the world, and provided almost an unlimited selection of topics and presentations to choose from: 

“All in all, it was great to see so many sociologists presenting, and so many topics explored. Nevertheless, due to the sheer size of the conference, it was only possible to visit four sessions per day. There were many occasions in which I was unable to attend sessions because I had committed to another one”, says Mark. 

“Another thing that I was surprised about was how much we live in our own sociological bubbles. The diversity and scope of the programme was a reminder that Sociology is indeed very fragmented. The conference offered a welcome opportunity to challenge one’s usual notions and get fresh ideas”, Michael adds.

title: Helsinki Animal Law Seminar: David John Holroyd 17.9.2026
content:
HALC seminar information

Time: Wednesday, September 17th, 15:00-16:00 (UTC +2 / Helsinki time)
Place: Apollo 129/online (register )

Doctoral researcher David John Holroyd (University of Sheffield)

"Animal politics: past, present future" 

Since the early 2010s, the “political turn” in animal ethics has challenged political theory’s longstanding indifference to nonhuman animals, sparking crucial debates on rights, representation, agency, and systemic transformation. 

Mapping the past, present, and future of the field, this talk reflects on how this literature in ‘Animal Politics’ has matured since its emergence. This includes evaluating its balance of normative and empirical theory, as well as clarifying the field’s relationship to neighbouring debates in animal law, animal ethics, and critical animal studies.

title: Nisäkästieteen päivät
content:
The events purpose is to bring together mammalogists, students, and mammal enthusiasts active in Finland, and to present the latest research results in the field as well as the full range of Finnish mammal research. The event is open to everyone, including media representatives. Speakers are mostly invited, but participants can also propose their own presentation, particularly in poster form.

The program consists of keynote talks, other presentations, and posters. Presentations are mostly in Finnish, with a length of 20+5 minutes. If a presenter's native language is not Finnish, the presentation and abstract may be in English. Posters may be in English. There is no restriction on poster size, but a good size is, for example, 80 x 110 cm (portrait). The poster session is on Friday afternoon. The event ends on Saturday afternoon.

title: Active Numeracy Welcomes Colleagues from Tallinn University
content:
Among the visitors were Professor Piret Soodla, Associate Professor Anna-Liisa Jõgi, Associate Professor Helin Puksand, Associate Professor Ene Varik-Maasik, Dr. Liina Malva, Veronika Kalle, Kristi Jakobson, and Kadrian Allika from Tallinn University. Their expertise spans mathematics learning difficulties, teacher education, inclusion, reading, language development, and classroom interaction.

The Active Numeracy seminar (11.9.26) was the second full-day event with the visitor from Tallinn. Read more about the first day (10.9.26) on the .

Dr. Heidi Hellstrand introduced the Functional Numeracy Junior (FUNA-jr) and Dyscalculia Battery (FUNA-DB) assessments, which are designed to identify children at risk of mathematical learning difficulties. The measures focus on number processing and arithmetic fluency, while also capturing fluency and processing speed through reaction times.
